blocks.title: A neighbourhood party in Montréal
blocks.context: Lucie, a volunteer, welcomes Nguyen, a newcomer. Later her neighbour Amira joins them.

lines.speaker: Lucie
lines.fr: Bonjour, monsieur ! Bienvenue ! Je m'appelle Lucie.
lines.en: Hello, sir! Welcome! My name is Lucie.

lines.speaker: Nguyen
lines.fr: Bonjour, madame. Enchanté. Moi, c'est Nguyen.
lines.en: Hello, ma'am. Nice to meet you. I'm Nguyen.

lines.speaker: Lucie
lines.fr: Pardon ? Vous pouvez répéter, s'il vous plaît ?
lines.en: Sorry? Can you repeat, please?

lines.speaker: Nguyen
lines.fr: Nguyen : N-G-U-Y-E-N.
lines.en: Nguyen: N-G-U-Y-E-N.

lines.speaker: Lucie
lines.fr: Merci ! Ravie de vous rencontrer. Vous venez d'où ?
lines.en: Thank you! Pleased to meet you. Where are you from?

lines.speaker: Nguyen
lines.fr: Je suis vietnamien. Je viens de Hanoï, au Vietnam. Et vous, vous êtes québécoise ?
lines.en: I'm Vietnamese. I'm from Hanoi, in Vietnam. And you, are you from Québec?

lines.speaker: Lucie
lines.fr: Oui, je viens de Québec. Mais maintenant, j'habite à Montréal. Et vous, vous habitez où ?
lines.en: Yes, I'm from Quebec City. But now I live in Montréal. And you, where do you live?

lines.speaker: Nguyen
lines.fr: J'habite à Montréal aussi, ici, dans le quartier.
lines.en: I live in Montréal too, here, in the neighbourhood.

lines.speaker: Lucie
lines.fr: C'est super ! Vous parlez bien français ! Vous parlez quelles langues ?
lines.en: That's great! You speak French well! What languages do you speak?

lines.speaker: Nguyen
lines.fr: Je parle vietnamien, anglais et un peu français. J'étudie le français à Montréal.
lines.en: I speak Vietnamese, English and a little French. I'm studying French in Montréal.

lines.speaker: Lucie
lines.fr: Bravo ! Euh… on se tutoie ?
lines.en: Well done! Um… shall we use tu?

lines.speaker: Nguyen
lines.fr: Oui, bien sûr ! Et toi, tu parles anglais ?
lines.en: Yes, of course! And you, do you speak English?

lines.speaker: Lucie
lines.fr: Un peu. Oh, voilà Amira ! Amira, je te présente Nguyen.
lines.en: A little. Oh, here's Amira! Amira, this is Nguyen.

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.fr: Salut, Nguyen ! Tu viens d'où ?
lines.en: Hi, Nguyen! Where are you from?

lines.speaker: Nguyen
lines.fr: Du Vietnam. Et toi ?
lines.en: From Vietnam. And you?

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.fr: Moi, je suis marocaine. Je viens de Casablanca.
lines.en: Me, I'm Moroccan. I'm from Casablanca.

lines.speaker: Nguyen
lines.fr: Ah bon ? Alors tu parles arabe ?
lines.en: Oh really? So you speak Arabic?

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.fr: Oui ! Arabe, français et anglais.
lines.en: Yes! Arabic, French and English.

lines.speaker: Nguyen
lines.fr: Trois langues ! Moi aussi !
lines.en: Three languages! Me too!

blocks.body:
This conversation uses everything from units 1 and 2. Listen once without the English, then once with it. Notice the moment Lucie and Nguyen switch from [[vous]] to [[tu]].

New words: [[vietnamien]] = Vietnamese (person or language), [[le Vietnam]] = Vietnam, so [[au Vietnam]] = in Vietnam and [[du Vietnam]] = from Vietnam; [[dans le quartier]] = in the neighbourhood; [[Bravo !]] = Well done!

blocks.title: The shape of a first conversation
blocks.body:
Most first conversations follow the same path. You already have the French for each step:

- **Greet:** [[Bonjour !]] / [[Bonsoir !]] / [[Salut !]]
- **Names:** [[Je m'appelle…]] / [[Moi, c'est…]], then [[Enchanté(e) !]]
- **Origin:** [[Je suis…]] (nationality), [[Je viens de…]]
- **City:** [[J'habite à…]]
- **Languages:** [[Je parle…]]
- **Keep it going:** answer, then ask back with [[Et toi ?]] / [[Et vous ?]]
- **Close:** [[Bonne journée !]], [[Au revoir !]], [[À bientôt !]]

You don't have to follow this order. But if you get stuck, the next step is always a question back.

answer
blocks.note: Pick **one** column and stay in it. Mixing [[tu]] and [[vous]] in the same question is the most common mistake.

head: situation
choose
English

a friend, a child, a classmate
un employé, un médecin, une personne âgée

blocks.note: When in doubt, start with [[vous]]. The other person will often suggest [[tu]].

blocks.title: Follow-up reactions
blocks.note: Short reactions make you sound natural and give you time to think.

examples.fr: Ah bon ? Tu viens du Maroc ?

examples.en: Me too! I live in Laval.

examples.fr: C'est super ! Et toi, tu parles espagnol ?
examples.en: That's great! And you, do you speak Spanish?

blocks.body:
- In Québec, people switch to [[tu]] **fast**, often after a few minutes and sometimes without asking. At work, colleagues usually say [[tu]] to each other. With a client, a doctor or a government office, keep [[vous]].
- [[Bienvenue !]] means “Welcome!” everywhere. In Québec it is also a common answer to [[merci]], like “You're welcome!” In France it isn't used that way: people say [[De rien !]], which is understood everywhere, including Québec.
- In everyday Québec speech you'll often hear [[Allô !]] as a friendly “Hi!”, not only on the phone.

- **Mixing tu and vous:** [[Tu habitez où ?]] is wrong. Say [[Tu habites où ?]] or [[Vous habitez où ?]]
- **Yes/no answers only:** [[Oui.]] stops the conversation. Add one detail and a question: [[Oui, j'habite à Laval. Et toi ?]]
- **Wrong verb:** nationality uses [[être]] ([[je suis mexicain]]), city uses [[habiter]] ([[j'habite à Montréal]]). [[Je suis à Montréal]] means you are in Montréal *right now*.
- **Little words:** [[à]] + city, [[en]] / [[au]] / [[aux]] + country, [[de]] / [[du]] after [[je viens]].

blocks.title: The 1 + 1 + 1 rule
blocks.body: For every question you get, give **1 answer**, add **1 detail**, and ask **1 question back**. This keeps any conversation going, even at A1.

examples.fr: — Tu habites où ? — J'habite à Gatineau, au Québec. Et toi ?
examples.en: — Where do you live? — I live in Gatineau, in Quebec. And you?

examples.fr: — Vous parlez anglais ? — Oui, couramment. Et un peu espagnol. Et vous ?
examples.en: — Do you speak English? — Yes, fluently. And a little Spanish. And you?

blocks.note: These short reactions are worth saying until they come out automatically.

blocks.title: A self-introduction
blocks.context: Raj introduces himself at the start of a volunteer meeting in Ottawa.
blocks.fr: Bonsoir à tous ! Je m'appelle Raj. Je suis indien, je viens de Delhi. Maintenant, j'habite à Ottawa, en Ontario. Je parle hindi, pendjabi et anglais. J'étudie le français, alors je parle un peu français. Enchanté !
blocks.en: Good evening, everyone! My name is Raj. I'm Indian, I'm from Delhi. Now I live in Ottawa, in Ontario. I speak Hindi, Punjabi and English. I'm studying French, so I speak a little French. Nice to meet you!

blocks.fr: Bonsoir à tous ! Je m'appelle Raj. Je suis indien, je viens de Delhi. Maintenant, j'habite à Ottawa, en Ontario. Je parle hindi, pendjabi et anglais. J'étudie le français, alors je parle un peu français. Enchanté !
blocks.explain: [[J'habite à Ottawa, en Ontario.]] Delhi is where he comes from: [[je viens de Delhi]].

steps.title: Mission: your first conversation
steps.intro: This is your unit 2 mission. Record yourself, then write. Use the checklist, then compare with the models.

blocks.prompt: At a welcome event, you meet someone new. Speak for about 45 seconds: greet them, give your name (and spell it), your nationality, where you come from, where you live, and the languages you speak. Ask at least two questions back, react to the answers, and suggest switching to tu.
checklist: Nationality (je suis…) and origin (je viens de…)
City with à, and province or country with en / au
A reaction: Ah bon ? / Moi aussi ! / C'est super !

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Bonjour ! Je m'appelle Karim, K-A-R-I-M. Je suis marocain, je viens de Casablanca, au Maroc. Maintenant, j'habite à Gatineau, au Québec. Je parle arabe, français et un peu anglais. Et vous, comment vous appelez-vous ? … Enchanté ! Vous habitez où ? … Ah bon ? À Gatineau ? Moi aussi ! … Et vous parlez quelles langues ? … C'est super ! On se tutoie ?
models.en: Hello! My name is Karim, K-A-R-I-M. I'm Moroccan, I'm from Casablanca, in Morocco. Now I live in Gatineau, in Quebec. I speak Arabic, French and a little English. And you, what's your name? … Nice to meet you! Where do you live? … Oh really? In Gatineau? Me too! … And what languages do you speak? … That's great! Shall we use tu?

blocks.prompt: Write a short self-introduction for the welcome page of your French class's online group (30 to 60 words). Include your name, nationality, where you come from, where you live, the languages you speak, and end with one or two questions for the group.
checklist: One or two questions with vous (the whole group)

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Bonjour à tous ! Je m'appelle Sofia et je suis mexicaine. Je viens de Monterrey, au Mexique. Maintenant, j'habite à Montréal, au Québec. Je parle espagnol et anglais, et je parle un peu français. J'étudie le français et j'aime le Canada ! Et vous, vous habitez où ? Vous parlez quelles langues ?
models.en: Hello everyone! My name is Sofia and I'm Mexican. I'm from Monterrey, in Mexico. Now I live in Montréal, in Quebec. I speak Spanish and English, and I speak a little French. I'm studying French and I love Canada! And you, where do you live? What languages do you speak?

models.label: Shorter model
models.fr: Salut ! Moi, c'est Mei. Je suis chinoise, je viens de Shanghai. J'habite à Vancouver, en Colombie-Britannique. Je parle mandarin, anglais et un peu français. Et vous, vous venez d'où ?
models.en: Hi! I'm Mei. I'm Chinese, I'm from Shanghai. I live in Vancouver, in British Columbia. I speak Mandarin, English and a little French. And you, where are you from?

summary:
- Hold a short first conversation: greeting, name, nationality, origin, city and languages
- Ask the key questions with **tu** or **vous**, and stay consistent
- Keep it going with [[Et toi ?]], [[Ah bon ?]], [[Moi aussi !]], [[C'est super !]]
- Suggest switching with [[On se tutoie ?]] and introduce someone with [[Je te présente…]]
